semantic_review.masked_select: The unchanged selected masked_select_kernel body is pasted directly with all seven statements, the original Bool cast, prefix subtraction, mask order and FP32 payload store. No separate Python candidate is authored: the existing equivalence compares two real autotune configurations of this same source, retaining all twenty choices. Pointer storage, unannotated runtime size and block constexpr remain outside the body. The signature records signed-int64 prefix storage and explicitly selects the existing natural-valued mathematical prefix channel. That choice requires an already typed Region.nat caller and validates distinct integer pointer names using non-unifying type inspection; it proves no native width, nonnegative value or storage bound. The unchanged prefix/cumsum, admission and native/IO refinement retain those obligations. The complete new ComputeKernel is proved identical to the previous FP32 TypedCopy source for every invocation, including all ports, statements and conversions; therefore arbitrary-state execution, failure, safety, output/frame, all configuration pairs and existing host/Tensor/native scopes are retained without a numerical identity or new premise. All nineteen task roots replay. The complete explicit-AST frontend unit keeps a Nat prefix load/subtraction and the FP32 store precision annotation; no extra floating cast is introduced. Negative guards reject floating/missing/duplicate names and a RegionName caller that has not already selected a natural channel. A standalone identical body using ordinary declared-int64 default channel correctly fails a complete-kernel identity with the explicitly chosen natural view, documenting representation rather than pretending storage metadata proves a range bound. Python mutation checks pin the int64 signedness, channel choice, Bool cast, subtraction, mask order and call metadata. No source dtype, public input domain, floating operation or numerical dependency changes.
